Extract Tidy Causal Inference Table from a TMLE Fit

Source: R/tidymodels_verbs.R
tidy.tmle_fit.Rd

Returns a publication-ready inference tibble containing point estimates, influence-function standard errors, test statistics, p-values, confidence intervals, optional simultaneous uniform confidence bands, and optional VanderWeele-Ding E-values.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tmle_fit'
tidy(
  x,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.level = NULL,
  simultaneous = FALSE,
  e_value = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted "tmle_fit" object.

conf.int

Logical; whether to include conf.low and conf.high columns (default TRUE).

conf.level

Confidence level for intervals; defaults to the level stored on x (0.95 initially unless changed via retarget()).

simultaneous

Logical; if TRUE and multiple estimands are present, computes simultaneous uniform confidence bands via a fast Rademacher wild multiplier bootstrap over the joint EIF matrix.

e_value

Logical; if TRUE, appends e_value and e_value_ci sensitivity columns (VanderWeele & Ding, 2017) quantifying robustness to unmeasured confounding.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A tibble::tibble().

Details

For additive contrasts ("ate", "att", "atc", "ey1", "ey0", and continuous Modified Treatment Policies), std.error is on the native outcome scale and intervals are symmetric Wald bounds. For ratio estimands ("rr" and "or"), std.error is reported on the log scale (SE[log(RR)] / SE[log(OR)]) and confidence intervals are computed on the log scale and exponentiated back so intervals remain strictly positive.

Examples

df <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 150, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 42)
fit <- tmle_spec(y, a, c(age, sex, lab_1, lab_2), estimand = c("ate", "rr", "or")) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 3L) |>
  fit(df)
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   estimand term  estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low
#>   <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 ate      ATE      0.209    0.0833      2.51  0.0120   0.0461
#> 2 rr       RR       1.88     0.253       2.49  0.0127   1.14  
#> 3 or       OR       2.59     0.382       2.49  0.0127   1.23  
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: conf.high <dbl>
tidy(fit, simultaneous = TRUE, e_value = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 11
#>   estimand term  estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low
#>   <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 ate      ATE      0.209    0.0833      2.51  0.0120   0.0401
#> 2 rr       RR       1.88     0.253       2.49  0.0127   1.12  
#> 3 or       OR       2.59     0.382       2.49  0.0127   1.19  
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: conf.high <dbl>, e_value <dbl>,
#> #   e_value_ci <dbl>, crit.value <dbl>
